research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: "It's almost 2026, and for the New Year, I'm going to blow up my car."
research_analysis.visual_hook: A young man beside a beat-up silver Corolla holding a lighter to a fuse that runs into the hood, with the text "Filled my car with fireworks".
research_analysis.narrative_structure: One-man two-character skit, 81 seconds, 22 cuts. Absurd visual premise in the first 3 seconds, then the car speaks. Shot and reverse-shot between the man and the car's grille. The car asks plain questions until the man admits his real reason, the car delivers a sincere point about spending to impress people, and he hugs the hood.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: An impossible conversation used to say something sincere. The car asks the questions a friend would be too polite to ask, so the confession ("I don't want people to think I'm broke") comes from the man, not from a lecture.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 1.5M views, 77.8x the 18.9K median listed for this account (5M followers; the caption says it is a trial reel repost). Every line is also on screen as text. Soft instrumental swells into the car's long speech. Ends on "I think it's wise to live more humbly in 2026".
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the first three seconds earn the stop, and the turn to sincerity at about 0:53 is what gets it shared, because people forward it to a friend who is about to overspend. The on-screen dialogue lets it work muted.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: It is a one-man character skit, the only acted format he has proven (2.8M on the client skit), and it uses his real car and his real job. Arguing with the car lets him be the fool while the car says the true thing about being 23.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: absurd opening image, the car as the voice of reason in shot and reverse-shot, a turn from comedy to one sincere line. New: no fire or fuse; the premise is a marketing guy about to tape a giant poster of his own face to his hood. The subject is vanity about looking successful, the dialogue is new, it ends on a joke instead of a hug, and it is half the length.

alex_adaptation.concept: Alex, a 23-year-old who gets brands views for a living, decides his Lexus should advertise him. He is about to tape a huge print of his own face to the hood when the car objects. The car wins the argument and then ruins the moment.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: Young entrepreneurs, people who bought something to look successful, and anyone who enjoys a marketing guy being humbled by a sedan.
alex_adaptation.first_frame: Alex standing at the front of the Lexus holding a poster-size print of his own grinning face flat against the hood, a roll of tape on his wrist, looking at the camera like this is a great idea.
alex_adaptation.first_spoken_line: I'm putting my face on my car. It's called marketing.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.dialogue: I'm putting my face on my car. It's called marketing.
full_script.action: Proud. Smooths the poster onto the hood with his forearm and tears a strip of tape with his teeth.
full_script.camera: Medium wide, tripod, front three-quarter of the car.
full_script.on_screen_text: Header: "Putting my face on my car". Dialogue captions throughout.
full_script.audio: Outdoor ambient. Tape-tearing sound up front.

full_script.speaker: Car
full_script.action: No movement. The grille and headlights fill the frame.
full_script.camera: Low, dead-center close-up of the front grille and badge.
full_script.on_screen_text: Caption in a different color for the car: "Absolutely not."
full_script.editing: Cut to grille. Use this same grille shot for every car line.
full_script.audio: Car voice: Alex's own voice pitched down slightly, calm, dry.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.action: Freezes with tape stuck to his lip. Looks at the grille, then at the camera, then back at the grille.
full_script.camera: Medium close on Alex, slightly high angle as if from the car's point of view.

full_script.speaker: Car
full_script.dialogue: You get people views for a living. On their phones. Why does your face need to be on my hood?

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.dialogue: Brand awareness. People see the car, they see me, they think: that guy's doing well.
full_script.action: Recovering his pitch voice. Gestures from the poster to himself to an imaginary crowd.

full_script.speaker: Car
full_script.dialogue: We went to Publix today. And the gym. Who is the audience? Brenda in produce?

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.action: Defensive, small. He knows it is weak as he says it.

full_script.speaker: Car
full_script.dialogue: You're twenty-three. You bought me because you wanted people to think you'd made it. You haven't made it. You've started. You're allowed to just be starting.
full_script.camera: Grille close-up, slow push-in over the whole line.
full_script.on_screen_text: Caption, one sentence at a time.
full_script.audio: Soft single piano note under the line. Car voice gentler.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.action: He takes it. Looks down at the poster of his own enormous grin. Quietly peels it off the hood, rolls it up, and tucks it under his arm. A small honest nod to the car.
full_script.camera: Medium on Alex, same high angle.
full_script.audio: Piano note rings out. Poster crinkle.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.dialogue: ...Can I at least do a small sticker?
full_script.action: Hopeful, pulling a tiny round sticker of his face from his pocket and holding it up between two fingers.

full_script.speaker: Car
full_script.dialogue: No. And while we're talking: premium. I've said premium.
full_script.camera: Grille close-up, then a 1-second wide of Alex walking to the driver's door with the rolled poster, muttering.
full_script.on_screen_text: Caption: "No. And while we're talking: premium."
full_script.editing: Cut to wide on 'I've said premium'. Hard out.
full_script.audio: Car voice. Door-open chime to end.

alternate_hooks: Text only, 2 seconds, over the poster going on the hood: "POV: you work in marketing and you just bought a car"
"I'm twenty-three, I own a marketing agency, and this car is about to become a billboard."
Open on the car's line first, over the grille: "Don't you dare." Then cut to Alex holding the poster.
alternate_endings: After the sincere speech, Alex nods, rolls up the poster and says: "That was really wise." Car: "I'm a Lexus. Thoughtfulness is standard."
Alex agrees, puts the poster away, gets in, and the last shot is the rear of the car driving off with the tiny face sticker already on the bumper.
alex_adaptation.caption: My car has better judgment than I do and it costs more to feed.
alex_adaptation.call_to_action: Optional end text: "Part 2: the car reviews my content"

production.location: A quiet parking lot or driveway, car facing the camera, even light on the front end.
props: Poster-size print of his own grinning face (24x36 inch, about $20 at a print shop)
Roll of painter's tape (will not mark paint)
Small round sticker of the same face
production.wardrobe: Agency-owner casual: clean tee, maybe a quarter-zip. One outfit.
shot_list: Medium wide front three-quarter: poster going on (4s) and the walk to the door (2s)
Low dead-center grille close-up, locked off, 60 seconds of clean plate including one slow push-in
Medium close on Alex from hood height: all of his lines and the silent peel-off, in order
Insert of the tiny sticker between his fingers
b_roll: Clean grille plate for all car lines
production.editor_instructions: Record car lines as voiceover afterwards and pitch down 2 to 3 semitones; keep it human, not a robot. Car captions in one color, Alex in white. The 5-second silent beat at 31 to 36s is the turn: do not shorten it or cover it with music. Use painter's tape only on paint.

variants_to_test: Alternate hook: Open on the car saying "Don't you dare."
Alternate payoff: "I'm a Lexus. Thoughtfulness is standard."
testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 3. Promote if 48h views reach 3x the trailing median and either follows or shares per 1,000 reached is top quartile. If it converts at 2x median follows on low views, re-cut to 30 seconds with the car's first line as the hook.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: The car reviews his content: Alex shows it a Reel, the car says "I've seen parking lots. That's not one."
The car on the 100K goal: Alex announces the deadline, the car asks how many followers that is per day
His laptop becomes the voice of reason about a 2 a.m. purchase or a new business idea

creative_confidence.rationale: It is the format he has proof for (one-man acted skit), it states his age and job inside the jokes, and the car character can return. The sincere line is short and immediately undercut, so it should not read as a lecture.
uncertainties: Reference comes from a 5M-follower account, so its view count says less about the format than a small-account outlier would.
44 seconds with 10 cuts is more edit work than his usual posts.
'Brenda in produce' is an invented stand-in name, not a real person; change the store to wherever he actually shops.
The honest beat depends on him playing it straight for five silent seconds.
